To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we curate a dataset of structural MRIs in a large and healthy population, train a deep learning age estimation model that outperforms previous studies and analyze the regional contribution to the predictions.

we have achieved superior age estimation performance, confirmed the efficacy of deep neural networks, demonstrated the added utility of large-scale training with more uniform age distribution and confirmed the association between divergence from chronological age and neuropsychological measures.

1) we train a deep neural network to estimate brain age using a heterogeneous large scale dataset (N 10158), 2) the model achieves high accuracy in estimating brain age (MAE 6.06 years, R 0.970), 3) we demonstrate the utility of brain age in life span cognitive function analysis
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a deep learning model to estimate brain age in a healthy population and the analysis of its predictive power in life span cognitive aging and disease diagnosis.
developing a robust and reliable brain age estimation framework and demonstrating its utility in aging analysis of neuropsychological functions.

the application of machine learning to the analysis of structural brain MRI data in the estimation of brain age and in the analysis of the relationship between brain age, chronological age, and cognitive function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we achieve superior age estimations with a larger and more uniformly distributed dataset than in previous studies, which is further validated on an independent dataset, and that the estimated age can be used to predict neuropsychological measures, which is further supported by regional attribution analysis.
we demonstrate that our method is superior to existing methods, and that it has utility for life span aging analysis and for neuropsychological measures.

our work demonstrates the efficacy of deep neural network based brain age estimations, and the added utility that is achieved by training with data in larger number and with more uniform distribution across life span than in previous studies, as well as the regional contribution to the age prediction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

our brain age estimates can be used as a biomarker of brain aging, which is predictive of cognitive function, and can potentially be utilized to identify at risk populations for neurodegenerative diseases.
our brain age estimation model is more accurate and more generalizable, and the regional contribution to the model is more informative than previous models.

the deep learning model trained on a healthy population of brain MRI data can accurately estimate the chronological age of an individual and the divergence from chronological brain age can serve as a valuable biomarker for various neurological diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of deep learning, large scale heterogeneous data, and feature attribution techniques is a powerful approach to brain age estimation, and the resulting brain ages are a valuable biomarker for brain aging.

the use of deep learning with large and uniform training data is an effective approach to brain age estimation, and that the estimated brain age can be used as a valuable biomarker for various neurological diseases.
deep learning is a promising tool to improve brain age estimation accuracy and to provide insights into the aging process.
